News / Crypto Briefing / Square switches on Bitcoin payments by default for eligible US merchants

Square switches on Bitcoin payments by default for eligible US merchants 1 min read

XYZ BTCUSD Square has turned on Bitcoin payments by default for eligible US businesses. Sellers did not have to raise a hand, fill out a form, or sit through a webinar. The feature costs merchants 0% in processing fees through December 31. After that, a flat 1% fee kicks in. Square, the payments platform owned by Block, Inc., began auto-enabling Bitcoin acceptance on March 30, 2026. The full rollout across eligible sellers is scheduled to be complete by November 10, 2026. That reach matters. Square's merchant network includes over four million sellers. Payments run over the Lightning Network, a layer built on top of Bitcoin designed for fast, cheap transactions. The practical upshot is near-instant settlement. By default, merchants receive US dollars. The Bitcoin a customer sends is converted automatically at the moment of payment. Sellers who actually want to hold Bitcoin can choose to keep it instead. The fee schedule is straightforward. Processing is free through December 31, 2026, and moves to a flat 1% starting January 1, 2027. There are guardrails. Individual transactions are capped at approximately $600, and each seller faces a daily ceiling of about $20,000. Geography also limits the reach. The service is unavailable in New York and certain other jurisdictions. On the hardware side, Square says no new equipment is needed. The feature plugs into existing tools like Square Register and Invoices, along with Square's apps. Square is also letting businesses convert up to 50% of eligible daily card sales into Bitcoin. The move reflects Block's ongoing effort to embed crypto into everyday commerce. CEO Jack Dorsey and Bitcoin product head Miles Suter are steering the initiative. The pitch tackles two complaints small businesses tend to have about accepting Bitcoin: volatility and operational hassle. Automatic dollar conversion addresses the first. Integration with existing Square tools addresses the second. Shifting from opt-in to on-by-default is the bigger philosophical change. For merchants, the near-term calculus is simple. Through December 31, accepting Bitcoin costs nothing in processing fees, requires no new hardware, and pays out in dollars unless the seller says otherwise. The approximately $600 transaction cap and roughly $20,000 daily ceiling limit high-value use cases, and the exclusion of New York and other jurisdictions shows regulation still shapes where this can operate.

News / Stock Story / Plug Power, JELD-WEN, Trex, GE Vernova, and Hertz shares are falling, what you need to know

Plug Power, JELD-WEN, Trex, GE Vernova, and Hertz shares are falling, what you need to know 2 min read

PLUG JELD TREX GEV

What happened? A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the Consumer Price Index increased 0.4 percent in October 2026, highlighting persistent price pressures across the economy. The latest inflation figures showed that underlying inflation remains resilient, with the core Consumer Price Index—which excludes volatile food and energy costs—advancing 0.3 percent over the month. Sticky inflation complicates corporate operating environments by elevating input costs and weakening consumer spending power. When consumer price gauges climb faster than expected, market participants often reassess future earnings expectations, particularly for high-growth technology firms whose future cash flows are heavily sensitive to macroeconomic headwinds. Sector-wide sentiment turned cautious as investors factored in the potential durability of elevated cost structures across operations. The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks. But moves this big are rare even for JELD-WEN and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business. The previous big move we wrote about was about 24 hours ago when the stock gained 12.1% on the news that falling crude oil prices fueled a broad market rebound and eased cost concerns surrounding artificial intelligence data center construction. CNBC reported that the major indexes rallied as oil prices dropped. In the session, Brent was down about 4% to around $94 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate was down about 3% to around $87. United States equities rallied to claw back losses from the prior week as retreating crude benchmarks alleviated inflationary headwinds across major industries. Lower energy prices are particularly advantageous for energy-intensive sectors, offering timely relief to developers scaling artificial intelligence facilities. Construction of hyperscale data centers requires substantial capital and power resources, making sustained high energy costs a threat to projected operating margins. As fuel costs swung lower, concerns regarding buildout budgets diminished, driving broad-based investor optimism across the technology and infrastructure ecosystem. JELD-WEN is down 58.3% since the beginning of the year, and at $1.04 per share, it is trading 67.5% below its 52-week high of $3.18 from January 2026.
